ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 3 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Arthur Ashe

text.paragraph: Mr. Ashe returns three months after his first visit, about seven months after starting antiretroviral therapy. He has missed no doses. He has had no headache, weakness, rash, fever, or chest pain. He is coaching four afternoons a week and hitting balls three times a week without angina. He has had no muscle aches on atorvastatin and ezetimibe. His blood tests were drawn this morning. He left before giving a urine sample, so the urine albumin test ordered at the last visit was not done. He feels more like himself and says that worry about his privacy comes and goes. [S]

list.item:
HIV infection (B20). Viral load not detected (below 20 copies/mL): the goal of therapy is reached. CD4 count 218, above 200 for the first time. Blood count normal: hemoglobin 13.6 g/dL, white cells 4.6, platelets 224. Potassium 4.7 mmol/L and creatinine 1.15 mg/dL, stable. Hepatitis B surface antibody 86 mIU/mL: protected. He was told that once the viral load has stayed undetectable for six months, HIV is not transmitted sexually. [S]
Continue the same regimen.
Viral load, CD4 count, metabolic panel, and urine albumin at six months.

Cerebral toxoplasmosis on maintenance therapy (B58.2). No symptoms. CD4 now above 200; maintenance can stop once it has stayed above 200 for more than six months. [S]
Continue trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole; reassess at the nine-month visit.

Hyperlipidemia (E78.5). LDL 52 mg/dL on atorvastatin and ezetimibe, below the goal of 55, from 88 at intake. Triglycerides 125, HDL 41. ALT 27 U/L. Lipoprotein(a) 24 mg/dL, not elevated. The recheck came 13 weeks after ezetimibe was added, one week outside the 4 to 12 week window, with no effect on care. [S]
Continue atorvastatin 80 mg and ezetimibe 10 mg.
Yearly lipid panel.

Coronary artery disease after two bypass operations (I25.10). No angina with regular vigorous exercise; blood pressure at goal. [S]
Continue aspirin and the chest-pain plan.
